name: Cutting

card.summary: A calorie-deficit phase to lose fat and show muscle and bone definition; a staple of looksmaxxing leanness advice.
card.note: Aggressive deficits carry muscle-loss and hormonal risks, and forum questions about cutting during puberty raise additional concerns.

quick.overview:
Cutting is eating in a calorie deficit to lose body fat while trying to keep muscle. In bodybuilding it is the phase before a contest, typically lasting a few months, and it is alternated with bulking.

In looksmaxxing it is the main way users try to lower body fat for a more defined face and body. Forums include many teenagers asking how aggressive a cut can be during puberty.
quick.mechanism: Intake is set below maintenance, usually with resistance training and high protein to preserve muscle. A larger deficit speeds loss but raises the risk of losing muscle. A Grokipedia summary cites deficits of about 10 to 20 percent below maintenance and a loss rate of 0.5 to 1 percent of bodyweight per week.
quick.risks: Larger deficits raise the risk of muscle loss, and the same summary links prolonged low energy availability to impaired hormonal function, fatigue and mood changes. Whether the cut is worthwhile if muscle is lost is described as unclear. Posts by minors asking about extreme deficits during puberty are common on forums.

lead: Cutting is a phase of eating in a net negative energy balance, a calorie deficit, to lose body fat while preserving as much muscle as possible.[1][2] In competitive bodybuilding, athletes typically spend an off-season building muscle and then cut for roughly 12 to 14 weeks before a contest.[1]

A larger deficit produces faster weight loss but increases the risk of losing muscle, and Wikipedia notes it is unclear whether enough lean mass can be retained for the overall process to be worthwhile.[1] A Grokipedia summary describes typical cuts of 8 to 16 weeks, a deficit of roughly 10 to 20 percent below maintenance, weekly loss of 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight, and high protein intake to protect lean mass.[2]

In looksmaxxing communities cutting is discussed as the route to a leaner, more angular face, often within the practice called leanmaxxing. Threads concern appetite suppression, carbohydrate restriction, the effect of dropping from the teens to low body fat percentages on looks, and especially cutting during puberty.[3][4][5]
infobox: About 0.5-1% of body weight per week (one summary)[2]

paras: Cutting is the fat-loss phase that follows a building phase in bodybuilding. Competitors also add cardio and eat below maintenance beforehand, and in the final stage use carbohydrate loading and dehydration to maximise definition for the stage.[1]
The term also appears in general weight-loss contexts, where calorie deficit is the core mechanism and weight loss can include lean mass such as muscle.[6]

A Grokipedia summary lists a daily deficit of about 300 to 500 kcal, avoiding deficits larger than 25 percent of maintenance, protein around 2.3 to 3.1 g/kg per day, and maintained resistance training volume with progressive loading to preserve muscle.[2] The summary also describes mini-cuts as short, more aggressive deficits lasting roughly 2 to 6 weeks, with much of the early weight loss being water and glycogen.[2]

The same summary reports that low energy availability, below about 30 kcal per kg of fat-free mass per day, has been linked to impaired gonadal and thyroid function over weeks, with possible fatigue, low libido, mood changes and in women menstrual irregularities.[2] It also lists electrolyte problems and disordered eating as mental-health and nutritional risks.[2]

No studies found specific to cutting for appearance in looksmaxxing contexts. Encyclopedic sources summarise broader research on protein intake and resistance training during energy deficits, but these were not examined as primary studies here.[2]

On looksmax.org, users ask how low calories can safely go while cutting at 16, with one teenager saying they want to cut as aggressively as possible without stunting growth.[3] Another 16-year-old describes cutting from 88 kg to 73 kg over several months and worrying about lost bone mass and height potential; a reply says a sensible deficit does not cause either.[4]
Other threads discuss cutting lowering appetite, cutting carbs and mood, and how much cutting from 16-17 percent to 11-13 percent body fat would change appearance.[5]

lore.intro: Cutting is framed as the way to reveal facial bone structure and muscle definition, and much discussion involves minors asking about deficits during puberty.[3][4][5]

claims.claim: Cutting during puberty can stunt growth or cost height and bone mass
claims.believers: Teenage posters fear that aggressive cuts will close growth plates early or reduce height potential, while some replies say a moderate deficit does not do this.[3][4]
claims.experts: The sources examined contain no studies on cutting in adolescents. General sources note that very large deficits carry risks of muscle loss and hormonal effects.[2]

claims.claim: Dropping to low body fat noticeably improves appearance
claims.believers: Posters ask how much cutting from around 16-17 percent to 11-13 percent would change their looks and report improved definition.[5]
claims.experts: No published study was found measuring changes in facial attractiveness from cutting in this range.

claims.claim: Aggressive deficits cause muscle loss and hormonal effects
claims.believers: Some posters report that cutting lowered their appetite, and one thread title describes cutting carbs as making the poster depressed.[7][8]
claims.experts: A Grokipedia summary reports that larger deficits and low energy availability are linked to muscle loss and impaired gonadal and thyroid function.[2]
